question.text: Will EU leaders at the 26–27 November 2026 Special European Council agree on additional EU financing for Ukraine's 2027 needs beyond the €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves on the European Council conclusions of the 26–27 November 2026 Special European Council, as published on the Council's meeting page and "Main results" page for that meeting (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/meetings/european-council/2026/11/26-27/), including any separate Ukraine text issued alongside them at that meeting and endorsed by heads of state or government (whether by all 27 or by a subset of them). It resolves YES if those texts state that EU leaders "agree" or "decide" that the EU will provide new financing to Ukraine for 2027 beyond the €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan, evidenced by at least one of: a stated amount of new EU money, a named new instrument or mechanism (such as a new EU loan for 2027), or an explicit commitment that the EU will make additional financing available; an agreement in principle counts even if the legal act is left to the Council to finalise, and it counts even if one or more member states opt out or do not participate. It resolves NO if no such statement appears — for example if leaders only "call for", "look forward to", "take note of", "welcome" or "invite further work" on Ukraine's 2027 financing, if they say they "will revert" to it later, if the only wording is a general commitment to "address" Ukraine's 2027 financing needs without an amount, named instrument or explicit commitment to provide financing, or if leaders merely endorse the Commission's 30 October 2026 proposal to approve the remaining €45 billion of the existing loan for 2027. Expected disbursements under instruments already agreed — the Ukraine Facility and its 2027 allocations, the European Peace Facility, or the 2027 tranche of the €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan — are not additional financing and do not count. If the Council's page for the meeting is unavailable, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the content of the conclusions will be used.
question.fine_print: An agreement counts even if no amount is specified, provided the texts commit the EU to providing new financing for Ukraine in 2027 beyond the €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan. Bilateral assistance pledged by individual member states outside an EU-level commitment does not count. The €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan is the limited-recourse loan established by Regulation (EU) 2026/467, disbursed in two €45 billion tranches covering 2026 and 2027. If the meeting is postponed or cancelled so that no conclusions or main results are published for a 26–27 November 2026 meeting, the question resolves NO.

research:
Nothing has settled this yet. The Commission is due to put forward a new €45 billion loan on 18 November. It needs unanimity and is tied to the 2028-2034 EU budget fight, with Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria all resisting.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: The Council's meeting page (consilium.europa.eu/en/meetings/european-council/2026/11/26-27/) returned HTTP 403, a browser-check wall, so I could not read it. No conclusions exist yet because the meeting has not happened. I found no draft conclusions in public reporting.
- 2026-11-10/11: Costa wrote to Merz: "We will address this issue in the Special European Council on 26-27 November." He also said the Commission would table a proposal before then. Note that the criteria say a bare commitment to "address" the issue counts as NO. [Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/eus-costa-keeps-ukraine-funding-talks-on-late-november-agenda-despite-merz-appeal/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question. No new proposal has been formally tabled yet. The Commission's 30 October proposal (COM(2026) 606) only covers the remaining €45 billion of the existing loan, which does not count. [EU Neighbours East](https://euneighbourseast.eu/news/latest-news/ukraine-support-loan-european-commission-adopts-proposal-to-approve-remaining-loan-amount-of-e45-billion-for-2027/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: The Financial Times reports, carried by many outlets, that the Commission will propose a new €45 billion loan on 18 November:
  - It would be guaranteed by the EU budget and use the same mechanism as the €90 billion loan: Ukraine repays only once Russia pays reparations.
  - It would cover about two-thirds of the roughly €70 billion 2027 gap.
  - It needs unanimity.
  - The Commission wants to tie it to the next EU budget (MFF) to protect it from future vetoes. An official said this "raises the stakes" but that the two issues "will not proceed in parallel."
  - Several reports say member states other than Czechia, Slovakia (and probably Hungary) would carry the cost, which suggests an opt-out structure like the existing loan's. [1news.az](https://1news.az/en/news/20261116105008321-Financial-Times-European-Commission-to-offer-Ukraine-a-45-billion-loan), [bankier.pl](https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/45-mld-euro-dla-Ukrainy-W-UE-narasta-spor-o-finansowanie-Kijowa-9229164.html), [farmer.pl](https://www.farmer.pl/fakty/nowe-finansowanie-dla-ukrainy-ke-chce-45-mld-euro-potrzebna-zgoda-wszystkich-panstw-ue,187161.html)
- 2026-11-16 (reported): Czech PM Babiš wrote to Costa that a Ukraine financing deal "cannot be a precondition for the adoption of the next EU budget." [1news.az](https://1news.az/en/news/20261116105008321-Financial-Times-European-Commission-to-offer-Ukraine-a-45-billion-loan)
- 2026-11-12/13: At the informal Dublin summit, Costa said leaders would discuss Ukraine's "financing needs for next year and beyond" on 26-27 November, based on the Commission's upcoming proposals. [Interfax-Ukraine](https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1236433.html), [RTÉ](https://www.rte.ie/news/ireland/2026/1113/1599056-eu-leaders-dublin/)
- 2026-11-10/11: Merz wrote to Costa calling new Ukraine aid an "essential prerequisite" for the MFF. Fico called this "textbook blackmail" and pointed to Slovakia's veto. Hungarian PM Péter Magyar, speaking in Berlin, also opposed linking the budget to Ukraine aid. Hungary, Slovakia, Czechia and Bulgaria have signalled they will not contribute. [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/10/eu-budget-battle-erupts-as-four-countries-defy-merz-over-ukraine-aid), [Liga](https://news.liga.net/en/war/news/fico-accused-merz-of-blackmail-over-aid-to-ukraine-and-threatened-a-veto)
- 2026-11-09: Dombrovskis said the Commission was preparing options for about €45 billion with all 27 contributing, and was "cautiously optimistic." [2eu.brussels](https://2eu.brussels/en/news/commission-prepares-options-for-around-45-billion-in-additional-eu-funding-for-ukraine-in-2027)
- 2026-10 (late): Brussels Signal reported that officials expect another loan raised on capital markets. If November fails, Costa said leaders would try again on 17-18 December. Costa wants a deal by year end. [Brussels Signal](https://brusselssignal.eu/2026/10/brussels-wants-ukraine-funding-deal-agreed-before-the-year-ends/), [Agence Europe](https://agenceurope.eu/en/bulletin/article/13968/15/eu-considers-new-loan-of-around-eur45-billion-for-ukraine-in-2027-amid-already-complex-budget-negotiations)
- 2026-10-17: Fico said Slovakia and Hungary will not fund EU aid for Ukraine in 2027. [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/17/8058496/index.amp)
- 2026-10-15/16: The October European Council did not agree the MFF. [1news.az](https://1news.az/en/news/20261116105008321-Financial-Times-European-Commission-to-offer-Ukraine-a-45-billion-loan)

## 4. Base rates
- Big Ukraine financing decisions have usually needed more than one summit:
  - **October 2025:** Leaders put off the reparations loan, but at the next summit, 18-19 December 2025, they agreed the €90 billion loan. That deal used joint borrowing, an MFF headroom arrangement, and opt-outs for Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/12/18/eu-summit-on-knife-edge-over-plan-to-fund-ukraine-using-russian-assets)
  - **December 2023:** Hungary blocked the €50 billion Ukraine Facility. It was agreed at a special summit on 1 February 2024. (From memory, not re-checked.)
  - **March 2026:** Orbán's veto held up the €90 billion loan's implementation, and Hungary and Slovakia refused to sign the Ukraine conclusions. [WTOP](https://wtop.com/europe/2026/03/eu-leaders-blast-viktor-orban-over-a-ukraine-loan-veto-accusing-him-of-playing-election-games/)
- Pattern: once a formal proposal exists, a deal often comes at the first or second summit after it. Here the proposal arrives only 8 days before the meeting.
- Since December 2025, Ukraine texts have often been adopted by 25 or 26 leaders rather than all 27. That still counts under the criteria.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the pre-collected markets match this question. They cover Ukraine associate membership, accession treaty signature and trilateral talks, all unrelated.
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market, or expert forecast, on a new EU Ukraine financing deal at the November 2026 summit.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-18: The Commission formally presents the new €45 billion loan proposal. Watch for its legal form (an MFF amendment needing unanimity) and whether it allows opt-outs.
- 18-25 November: Ambassadors (Coreper) prepare the draft conclusions. Leaks will show whether the wording says "agrees" or "decides", which counts, or "calls for", "will revert" or "address", which does not.
- Watch the positions of Fico, Babiš, Magyar and Bulgaria: veto threats against an opt-out structure, and how they bargain over the MFF link.
- 26-27 November: Special European Council (MFF plus Ukraine 2027). If it fails, the fallback is 17-18 December, which would mean NO for this question.
- Meanwhile finance ministers may approve the 2027 tranche of the existing loan, but that does not count.

## 4. Base rates
- The closest precedent is the €90bn loan:
  - 2025-10-23: leaders committed to meet Ukraine's 2026-27 needs and invited the Commission to present options, without Hungary. [Sofia Globe](https://sofiaglobe.com/?p=125237)
  - 2025-12-18/19: leaders agreed the €90bn joint-debt loan at the regular December summit, after the reparations-loan plan failed, with Czechia, Hungary and Slovakia opting out. [Euronews](https://euronews.com/my-europe/2025/12/19/eu-to-issue-90-billion-in-joint-debt-for-ukraine-after-hitting-a-wall-on-reparations-loan)
  - From Commission options to a leaders' deal took about two months, and the deal came at a December summit.
- Large EU financing decisions for Ukraine have often needed two summits:
  - The €50bn Ukraine Facility failed in December 2023 and was agreed at a special summit on 1 Feb 2024.
  - That special summit is one precedent for a special European Council actually delivering a decision.
- This time the proposal arrives 8 days before the summit. The opt-out route used for the €90bn loan (separate guarantees with the three states exempted, then enhanced cooperation) shows a deal can count even without all 27. The FT, however, says the new loan needs unanimity.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) The summit is on 26-27 November 2026, so the outcome should be known within about 11 days (resolution around 28 November). For YES, the conclusions, or a Ukraine text endorsed by 25-27 leaders, must say leaders "agree" or "decide" that the EU will provide new 2027 financing beyond the €90bn loan. That means a stated amount, a named new instrument such as a new €45bn loan, or an explicit commitment to provide the money.

(b) Status quo: no new financing has been agreed, no formal proposal exists until 18 November, and four states (HU, SK, CZ, BG) oppose contributing. If nothing changes, the conclusions would likely contain "discuss", "address" or "will revert to" language and the issue would roll over to 17-18 December. That resolves NO.

(c) Base rate: major new EU Ukraine financing deals usually take two summits after a proposal.
- The €50bn Ukraine Facility failed in December 2023 and passed in February 2024.
- The reparations loan was deferred in October 2025, and the €90bn deal came in December 2025.
- The share agreed at the first summit after the proposal was tabled is roughly 25-35%. With only 8 days between proposal and summit, it is lower, about 20-25%.

(d) Evidence for YES:
- 16 November (FT): the Commission will table a concrete €45bn loan on 18 November, using the proven €90bn structure with opt-outs for CZ, SK and HU, which counts under the criteria.
- 9 November: Dombrovskis said he was "cautiously optimistic".
- Merz and Germany are pressing hard for an early decision.
- Since December 2025, Ukraine texts adopted by 25 or 26 leaders have been common.

Evidence for NO:
- The loan needs unanimity and is tied to the MFF, which is aimed at December.
- 10-11 November: Fico called the linkage "blackmail" and threatened a veto. Babiš wrote (reported 16 November) that Ukraine financing cannot be a precondition for the MFF. Magyar opposes the link.
- Bulgaria is also seeking an exemption.
- 10 November: Costa's wording was "address". 12 November: the joint statement said "discuss".
- 13 November: officials openly name 17-18 December as the fallback.
- Some pro-Ukraine states have reservations about Merz's approach.

(e) NO scenario: the proposal lands on 18 November and Coreper cannot settle the opt-out and MFF linkage in a week. The conclusions "take note of the Commission's proposal" and say leaders "will revert in December", where the package is closed alongside the MFF.

YES scenario: the holdouts accept a December 2025-style deal, with no contribution in exchange for not blocking. The conclusions read "The European Council agrees that the EU will provide an additional loan of up to €45 billion for 2027", with the legal act left to the Council.

(f) I start at about 22%. A concrete proposal and strong German pressure push this up a little. Moving up is limited because the MFF linkage makes a package deal in December the natural endpoint, there are four holdouts, unanimity is required, and the timeline is short. I also allow some chance that the conclusions use "agree in principle" wording, which counts. Net, I land at about 22%.

Probability: 22%

(a) About 11 days remain; the summit is on 26-27 November 2026 and conclusions follow immediately. For YES, the conclusions (or a separate Ukraine text endorsed by 25-27 leaders) must say leaders "agree" or "decide" that the EU will provide new 2027 financing beyond the €90bn loan. That means a stated amount, a named new instrument such as a new ~€45bn loan, or an explicit commitment to make additional financing available. Wording such as "address", "will revert" or "look forward to" means NO.

(b) Status quo: there is no agreement and no formal proposal yet. The Commission tables it on 18 November, only 8 days before the summit. Leaders lean towards revisiting in December, so the status quo is NO.

(c) Base rate: large new EU financing decisions for Ukraine rarely land at the first summit after a proposal. The €50bn Ukraine Facility failed in December 2023 and passed in February 2024. The reparations loan was deferred in October 2025, and the €90bn loan was agreed in December 2025, about two months after the options were presented. A proposal made 8 days before a summit and tied to an unresolved MFF has a first-summit success rate of perhaps 20-25%.

(d) Evidence:
- For YES:
  - The FT reported on 16 November that the Commission will propose a concrete €45bn budget-guaranteed loan using the existing mechanism.
  - Dombrovskis said on 9 November he was "cautiously optimistic".
  - Merz is pushing hard, and Costa kept the item on the November agenda.
  - The €90bn precedent shows an opt-out structure, without Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary, can still produce a qualifying agreement in principle, which would count.
- For NO:
  - Unanimity is reportedly needed for the budget guarantee.
  - Fico refused to participate (17 October and 10 November) and called the MFF link blackmail.
  - Babiš wrote on 16 November that Ukraine financing cannot be a precondition for the MFF.
  - Hungary and Bulgaria are also resisting.
  - The MFF itself is expected only in December, and the Commission wants the two linked.
  - On 10 and 12 November Costa spoke only of "address" and "discuss".
  - December is openly signalled as the fallback.

(e) NO scenario: the MFF talks stall and the holdouts refuse budget headroom for the loan. The conclusions say leaders "held a strategic discussion" and "will revert in December", or commit to "address" Ukraine's 2027 needs. YES scenario: under German pressure, 25 leaders sign a Ukraine text saying they "agree" in principle on a new €45bn loan for 2027 with opt-outs for CZ, SK and HU. Finalisation is left to the Council and tied to the December MFF.

(f) I start from a base rate of about 22%. I nudge it up slightly for the concrete proposal and the strong political push. I nudge it down for the very short timeline, the MFF linkage making a package deal in December more natural, and the strict wording criteria. Even a vague "commit to meet needs" formula would likely resolve NO. I land at about 20%.

Probability: 20%

(a) About 11 days remain; the summit is on 26-27 November and resolution is around 28 November. For Yes, the conclusions, or a separate Ukraine text endorsed by all 27 leaders or a subset, must say leaders "agree" or "decide" that the EU will provide new 2027 financing beyond the €90bn loan. That text must give an amount, name an instrument (such as a new €45bn loan), or explicitly commit the EU to providing additional financing. Wording such as "address", "will revert" or "invite further work" does not count.
